summary: Customer is developing a hot polymer extrusion process incorporating an active pharmaceutical ingredient and wants to investigate whether an optical measurement can detect composition changes in the melt during processing. They have offline assays, note a hot process interface with possible material build-up, and request an initial comparison plan and pre-probe questions.

unknowns: Which composition changes must be detected (for example active pharmaceutical ingredient concentration, polymer ratio, additive level, or degradation products) and over what concentration range.
The required accuracy, precision, limit of detection, response time, and measurement frequency.
The polymer matrix, additive package, active pharmaceutical ingredient loading, and likely spectral interferences.
The optical regime of the melt (clear, turbid, opaque, or opaque/absorbing) and whether it changes during processing.
Whether any fluorescent species or suitable fluorescent indicator is present.
The process temperature, pressure, flow rate, and installation point.
The interface geometry, distance from the process, and access for a probe.
Expected material build-up rate, cleaning method, and fouling tolerance.
Details of the offline assays, including sampling, comparability to the melt state, and reference accuracy.
Acceptance criteria and experimental design for the initial comparison plan.
